# File-authority denial messages now bounded and home-redacted

## What changed

Every `WRITE BLOCKED: Agent "…" is not authorised to write "…"` denial thrown by the shell
write gate and the file-write path now renders the target through one shared
bounded-and-redacted helper (`sanitizeDiagnosticText(redactPath(target), 320)` with the
escaping-relative home fold below), replacing raw interpolation at all four throw sites
(universal deny prefix, lenient verifier-config, enforced authority, and the non-shell
file_write door — agent names are bounded there too).

The shared `redactPath` now classifies profile shapes **lexically** on a normalized
slash form, on every host: normalization-created home paths (`/tmp/../home/<name>/…`,
`/home//<name>/…`) fold, exact profile roots (`/home/<name>`, `/Users/<name>`,
`C:\Users\<name>`) fold, and Windows-drive and UNC profile forms fold in either separator
flavor even on POSIX hosts (`C:/Users/<name>/…`, `//server/Users/<name>/…`). A folded
Windows path renders `~\rest` (the old `~\\rest` double separator is gone); non-profile paths
render exactly as before.

The file-authority denial **reason** keeps its workspace-relative display: an ESCAPING
relative path (normalized form starting `../`, provably outside the workspace) folds its
`home/<name>` / `Users/<name>` segment to `~`, and every other display routes through
`redactPath`. The denial message's target slot makes the same escaping decision on the
normalized form (`./../home/<name>/…`, `src/../../home/<name>/…`, and win32
`..\Users\<name>\…` all fold), so for operand-shaped targets — the non-shell file_write door —
the message and reason agree. The three SHELL doors render the RESOLVED absolute target: its
leading runtime profile folds, but an interior caller-supplied `home/<name>` segment beyond it
stays visible in the message while the reason folds it (folding interior segments of resolved
paths would over-redact legitimate in-workspace denial targets). Ordinary in-workspace relative
paths and non-home absolutes render structurally unchanged — through `redactPath`'s
host-normalized form, as before (over-redaction is pinned against).

Known bounds: when the workspace sits under one profile and the target under a SIBLING profile,
the relative display's common-ancestor prefix already dropped the `Users` segment, so the
sibling account name remains in the reason (the message's target slot is still folded); the
escaping fold is case-sensitive (`Users` but not `users`); a drive-relative win32 spelling
(`C:..\Users\<name>\…`, no separator after the drive) is not recognized as escaping, so the
message renders it raw while the reason folds it; and the lstat-failed / symlink-junction
ancestor denial arms still render the raw ancestor path (pre-existing, tracked for a
follow-up).

Diagnostic-only change: `ShellWriteBlockedError.writeTarget` stays exact; audit rows keep
their redacted-and-truncated contract and pick up the same profile folds (ordinary paths
persist unchanged); message shape is unchanged, so downstream message-parsing and the pinned
denial suites are unaffected.

## Why

Follow-up from PR #3568's final critic (#3587): a long attacker-influenced target (400+ chars)
flowed unbounded and un-redacted into denial messages — including absolute user-profile paths
(`C:\Users\<name>\…`) rendered verbatim. The PR #3567 round had fixed exactly one of the five
denial-throw sites; this closes the remaining four plus the reason channel.

Issue: #3587

# Neutralize control characters in swarm-residue inventory names (#3542)

## What changed

`formatResidueInventoryLines` in `src/services/swarm-residue.ts` now strips
C0/C1 (Unicode `Cc`) control bytes from entry names before the existing
backtick neutralization, matching the `safeName` shape that
`src/commands/doctor-store-integrity.ts` shipped in PR #3533. The residue
inventory sections of the `/swarm config doctor` read-only report and the
close dry-run report render through this one shared renderer. A new pinning
test, `tests/unit/services/swarm-residue-control-char-names.test.ts`, covers
`\n` row-injection, ESC terminal-pollution, DEL, NEL, a control byte inside a
directory component of a multi-segment path, VT (U+000B), and CSI (U+009F)
names, pins the exact rendered output for a crafted name (and the verbatim
name span for an ordinary name), and asserts the directory component survives
rendering (no over-stripping).

## Why

`relPath` values come from `readdir` of attacker-influenced trees. The old
renderer only replaced backticks, so a crafted entry name containing `\n`
could inject forged inventory rows into the report, and an ESC byte could
pollute terminal rendering. Quarantine actions were never affected by this
renderer defect (the quarantine move path is untouched by this change); the
defect class was bounded to report-line injection and terminal pollution. PR
#3533 fixed the identical class in the doctor store-integrity report — this
closes the surviving copy in the residue inventory renderer.

## Migration steps

None. The change is internal to report formatting; no config, state, or data
migration is involved. The residue-inventory sections of the doctor report
and the close dry-run report no longer carry raw control bytes in entry
names.

## Known caveats

- Control bytes are stripped, not escaped: a name `a\nb` renders as `ab`.
  This matches the shipped doctor-store-integrity behavior and is the
  intended minimal fix.
- The `Cc` strip also covers C1 control bytes (U+0080–U+009F), consistent
  with the PR #3533 precedent.
- Coverage bound: this fix covers the shared residue-inventory renderer only.
  Three sibling render surfaces still emit the same `relPath` values raw
  (no control-byte strip, and two of them no backtick neutralization either):
  the `--quarantine-residue` preserved list (`src/commands/doctor.ts`),
  the close clean-stage preserved-candidates warning (persisted verbatim
  into `.swarm/close-summary.md`), and the close dry-run archive/post-mortem
  name lists. Those sites predate this PR and are tracked for a follow-up.

# PR-workflow observability appends: fail-open lock escape and same-revision stale overwrite

## What

Two integrity fixes to the PR-workflow gate's observability-only append path
(rejection journals, skill-contract advisories, and the PR_FEEDBACK
base-mismatch marker), closing #3232 and the remaining scope of #3231.

- **Advisory append honours its fail-open contract under lock contention
  (#3232).** `appendPrWorkflowSkillContractAdvisories` documents that any
  error drops the append silently, but its protective `try` sat inside the
  session-state lock callback, so a lock-acquisition timeout (another process
  holding the lock for the full retry budget) escaped as a rejected promise.
  Its only caller is the auto-resume wake path, which then aborted before
  sending the resume prompt. The lock acquisition now sits inside the
  fail-open boundary, matching the three sibling observability writers; the
  wake continues and the resume prompt is sent.
- **A stale observability append can no longer erase an interleaved one
  (#3231).** Observability appends deliberately never advance the gate state
  `revision` (#3199), so two appenders holding snapshots at the same revision
  were indistinguishable to the write CAS: the second, built from a snapshot
  that predates the first, replaced the whole row and silently erased the
  first app

# Shell Write Gate: Directory State, Child-Scoped Chdir Wrappers, sh -c Payload (G1)

## What changed

- **Directory-state model for the write gate** (`src/hooks/shell-write-detect.ts`):
  the resolver walk now threads one `DirectoryState` (`{cwd, prevCwd, dirStack}`)
  through both passes instead of a bare cwd stack. `cd` word forms resolve-or-
  withdraw: bare `cd` / `cd ~` / `cd ~/x` land at `$HOME` (withdrawn when the
  line reassigns `HOME=`), `cd -` lands at the modeled `prevCwd` (withdrawn
  when unmodeled or `OLDPWD=` is reassigned), and dynamic operands (`cd $VAR`)
  withdraw later writes — the historical literal-append could fail OPEN under
  a broad declared scope. `pushd`/`popd` are tracked (push, bare swap, pop;
  `±N`/`-n`/stack-overflow withdraw), and `cd -P src` / `cd -- src` now track
  the real operand. Conditionals carry both outcomes explicitly: pipelines
  run components on isolated state copies with post-pipeline withdrawal,
  `if`/`case` branch copies diverge over the COMPLETE state (cwd + prevCwd +
  dirStack + withdrawal flag — #3567 feedback PRR-001) and withdraw, loops
  accept only a full-state fixpoint, and function bodies walk a discarded
  copy that inherits (never zeroes) the context withdrawal. Withdrawn writes reach the gate as
  `resolvedPath: null` with an additive `unresolved` marker; a withdrawn
  capability eval denies before any `evalDirectory` fallback (#3491 AC1/AC3,
  #3539 AC1/AC5).

- **Child-scoped env/sudo chdir through a quoted subshell transform**
  (`src/hooks/guardrails/destructive-command.ts`, `tool-before.ts`,
  `guardrail-explain-service.ts`): chdir-bearing wrapper segments
  (`env -C DIR`, `env -S '…-C DIR…'`, `sudo -D DIR`) rewrite at the gate as
  correctly-quoted subshells `( cd -- 'DIR' && <re-unwrapped inner> )`, so the
  wrapped command's writes resolve under the CHILD cwd while following
  siblings stay at the parent cwd (bash-true). DIR is emitted through a POSIX
  single-quote serializer (`'` → `'\''`); expansion-bearing operands
  (`$VAR`, `~`, `$(…)`, globs) are never serialized — the segment rewrites to
  a withdrawal form whose inner writes withdraw. Nested chdir wrappers
  compose as nested subshells. The destructive arm receives an evolving
  per-segment directory context (inner `cd`s tracked; unrepresentable
  mutations relocate to a deny-on-uncertainty sentinel), and
  `/swarm guardrail explain` shares the same preprocessing (#3491 AC2/AC4).

- **Shared `sh -c` payload extractor** (`src/hooks/guardrails/destructive-command.ts`):
  the payload is the single quote-removed word the `-c` flag selects (sh's
  argv[2] contract: the next standalone word after the flag cluster),
  extracted by a quote-aware tokenizer shared with the W2 serializer.
  Trailing positionals (`sh -c 'payload' sh`) and same-kind quote
  concatenation (`'\''`) no longer defeat the unwrap, and words after the
  payload ($0/$1…) are never scanned as commands (#3491 AC5/AC7).

- **Review round 1 hardening** (`destructive-command.ts`, `tool-before.ts`,
  `guardrail-explain-service.ts`): the uncertain-DIR withdrawal form uses a
  synthetic dynamic cd operand, so it withdraws UNCONDITIONALLY — the first
  round's synthetic `cd -` landed at a modeled `OLDPWD` after a preceding
  `cd`/`pushd` and admitted the wrapped writes. The destructive arm's
  child-cwd context is keyed per OCCURRENCE instead of per segment text
  (first-wins text keying let `env -C src rm -rf dist; env -C .. rm -rf
  dist` inherit the first occurrence's in-scope context). `/swarm guardrail
  explain` mirrors the gate's null-path decision tree — withdrawn/dynamic
  write targets answer block, and inspectable evals route through their
  tracked working directory exactly like the gate.

- **sh-family flag-cluster payloads** (`src/hooks/shell-write-detect.ts`,
  `src/hooks/guardrails/destructive-command.ts`; final-critic rounds 2–5):
  the covered grammar is bash-true, complete over four dim

## Guardrails: verifier-config protection for every role, unconditional under `guardrails.enabled=false` (#3120)

`.secretscanignore` and every built-in verifier-config glob (`tsconfig*.json`,
`biome.json(c)`, `.eslintrc*`, `eslint.config.*`, `.prettierrc*`,
`prettier.config.*`, `oxlintrc*`, `.golangci*`) are now denied for **every
agent role** — including the OpenCode-native roles (`general`/`build`/`plan`/
`explore`) previously exempt from swarm write restrictions — and the denial
fires **even with `guardrails.enabled: false`** (and in observe contexts):
these files are owner policy for the verification system itself (the secretscan
Stage-A gate trusts `.secretscanignore`), so their integrity is not switchable
by the general enforcement knob. The shell path additionally routes no-scope
lenient roles through the verifier-config check (native-role `echo x >
.secretscanignore` via bash is blocked). Disclosed boundary: script runners
(`npm run <script>`, `bun run <script>`, `node <file>`) remain NOT treated as
shell write vectors — their targets are not statically knowable and blocking
them would break every legitimate build; see the `shell-write-detect` module
documentation.

## Shell write detection: patch, checkout-ref, rsync vectors (#3120)

`git apply` / `patch` (explicit `-p<n>`; both diff endpoints so a rename/delete
of a protected preimage cannot hide behind the postimage; closed option set —
`--directory`, `-d`, `-o`, `-r`, backup options, and index-writing modes
`--cached`/`--index`/`--3way` fail closed; `patch` without explicit `-p` fails
closed because GNU patch then picks basenames itself), `git checkout <ref>
<pathspec>…` (no `--`), and `rsync <src>… <dest>` are now detected as write
vectors and authorized per-target through the cd-tracking resolver. Targets
named inside a patch are extracted at authorization time from the patch file
(bounded read): tab- and space-prefixed `---/+++` headers, C-style octal
escapes (`\ooo` — accumulated as bytes and decoded once as UTF-8; unknown
escapes and undecodable sequences fail closed), all four quoted/unquoted
`diff --git` header combinations (git quotes each name independently
under its default `core.quotePath=true`), pure
rename sections (`rename from`/`rename to` — no `---/+++` lines), and
rename/delete endpoints that only exist as section headers. Patch targets
are judged under BOTH landings (git apply is patch-root-relative, GNU patch
is cwd-relative), and `rsync` also flags `--exclude`/`--include`/`--filter`
arguments as write paths. Unreadable/undecodable patches and stdin patches
block.

## PR_FEEDBACK: durably bound merge base + Stage A trust screens (#3396)

- PR_FEEDBACK activation resolves the merge base via ONE bounded `gh pr view`
  and durably binds `prFeedbackBaseRef/Sha` in gate state (fail-open: a
  resolution failure records `prFeedbackBaseBindingError` and never wedges
  activation; a failed binding is retried on the next matching re-activation
  and a successful re-resolution clears the stale advisory). The bound value
  is the real merge base (`git merge-base base_ref pr_head_sha`), not the
  base-branch tip, so callers whose base advanced keep trusted provenance.
  The `gh` subprocess runs BEFORE the checkout/session mutation locks so the
  network call never stalls concurrent gate mutations. Stage A verifies its
  caller-asserted `base_sha` against the binding: matching runs carry the
  root-level `prFeedbackStageABaseTrust: 'binding-verified'` verdict; a
  differing base ignores the caller provenance entirely (trusted
  base-identical scripts unavailable — identical to no-provenance) and
  persists a bounded `prFeedbackStageABaseMismatch` marker (durable-wins
  evidence, appended without advancing the gate revision, cleared by a head
  rebind). The receipt's strict child keeps the BASE two-value trust floor
